answer: A sybil farm's shells all run from one operator's machine, so let geography do the talking. Each epoch, a few unannounced lantern audits flash across the network: the chosen identity must, within minutes, gather co-signatures from peers scattered across five distinct regions — proof of real-world distribution. One script cannot stand in five places at once, and faking it per shell needs genuine presence in each region, so the farm's cost spirals past its profit. Shells that only ever vouch for each other from the same ferrous rack betray their sameness, and the audit reclaims their rewards.
